eng_base_salary.label: Backend or infra engineer, base salary

source.title: BLS Occupational Outlook: software developers, median annual wage

eng_base_salary.note: US median for software developers. Infra specialists run higher; the median is the defensible default.

loaded_multiplier.label: Benefits multiplier on base salary

source.title: BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, private industry

loaded_multiplier.note: Private-industry total compensation divided by wages: benefits are 30% of compensation.

overhead_multiplier.label: Overhead multiplier (equipment, office, software)
overhead_multiplier.note: ECEC excludes non-compensation overhead. A conservative allowance, editable.

default_hours_accounts.label: Engineering hours a week on accounts, where the sliders start
default_hours_accounts.note: The form's bands (0, 1 to 10, 11 to 40, over 40) are read as 0, 5, 25 and 60 hours a week. The slider starts on the band nearest this; a results link that gives no band uses it directly.

default_hours_content.label: Engineering hours a week on user content, feeds and the graph, where the sliders start

default_hours_infra.label: Engineering hours a week on infrastructure and storage, where the sliders start

default_hours_legal.label: Engineering hours a week on legal and compliance work, where the sliders start
default_hours_legal.note: Deletion flows, export tooling, retention jobs. Same bands as above.

ts_base_salary.label: Trust and safety analyst, base salary

source.title: Payscale: Trust and Safety Analyst salary

ts_base_salary.note: Payscale median 70,480; Glassdoor average 101,409 (small samples, self-reported).

moderator_base_salary.label: In-house content moderator, base salary

source.title: Payscale: Content Moderator hourly rate

moderator_base_salary.note: Payscale median 20.44 per hour over 2,080 hours.

moderator_seat_outsourced.label: Outsourced moderation seat, all-in

source.title: 365outsource: content moderation outsourcing rates

moderator_seat_outsourced.note: Offshore list price about 8 per hour over 2,000 hours; US BPO 15 to 25 per hour. List prices, not contracts.

mods_per_million_mau.label: Moderators per million monthly users

source.title: Snap DSA transparency report H2 2025 (human resources and AMAR files)

mods_per_million_mau.note: From DSA transparency reports: LinkedIn about 3, Pinterest at most 5, Snap about 15 per million EU users. Used when the form gives no reviewers at all.

blob_gb_month.label: Object storage

source.title: AWS Price List API, Amazon S3 us-east-1

blob_gb_month.note: S3 Standard first 50 TB. Low is Backblaze B2; high is GCS multi-region.

db_gb_month.label: Database storage

source.title: AWS Price List API, Amazon RDS PostgreSQL gp3 us-east-1

db_gb_month.note: RDS PostgreSQL gp3 Multi-AZ. Low is single-AZ; high is Multi-AZ with readable standbys. Compute instances are extra and not modelled here.

egress_gb.label: Egress to the internet

source.title: AWS Price List API, data transfer out to the internet

egress_gb.note: AWS first 10 TB. Low is Cloudflare R2 (zero); high is Google Cloud.

egress_gb_per_mau_month.label: Egress per active user

source.title: Ericsson Mobility Report key figures (22 GB per smartphone per month, all apps)

egress_gb_per_mau_month.note: No platform publishes bytes served per user. The only proxy is 22 GB per smartphone per month across all apps.

db_mb_per_mau.label: Graph and profile metadata per user
db_mb_per_mau.note: Follows, profile, indexes and counters. Editable.

db_kb_per_post.label: Metadata per post or message, retained twelve months
db_kb_per_post.note: Row plus indexes, not the media. Retention of twelve months is a model constant.

compute_per_mau_year.label: Serving and feed compute per active user

source.title: Pinterest FY2025 Form 10-K: cost of revenue and MAU

compute_per_mau_year.note: Derived: Pinterest cost of revenue is 1.36 per MAU-year and Reddit 1.60 per DAU-year (both include hosting, ops staff and fees); Snap infrastructure alone is 3.40 per DAU-year. The typical value nets out storage and egress, which this model counts separately.

feed_compute_share.label: Share of that compute spent on feeds and recommendations

relay_cost_year.label: Running one relay of your own

source.title: Third-party estimates of Bluesky relay and PDS hosting cost

relay_cost_year.note: Third-party hosting estimates for a Bluesky relay or PDS run 30 to 512 per month. A Nostr relay with AUTH and rate limits sits in the same band.

media_sponsor_share.label: Media hosting an app still sponsors after moving to Nostr
media_sponsor_share.note: Blossom or similar: users can host their own media, apps often still pay for some of it.

cache_per_mau_year.label: A thin cache in front of relays
cache_per_mau_year.note: What a Nostr app still serves itself.

auth_per_mau_month.label: Authentication as a service

source.title: Google Cloud Identity Platform pricing

auth_per_mau_month.note: Identity Platform 100k to 1M tier. Low is its 10M-plus tier; high is Clerk beyond 50k.

reset_cost.label: Cost of one password reset

source.title: BleepingComputer, citing Forrester on helpdesk password resets

reset_cost.note: Self-service email or SMS plus a share of support. The 70-dollar figure often cited from Forrester is for enterprise helpdesks and is not used.

verify_price.label: Identity or age verification

source.title: Stripe Identity pricing

verify_price.note: Stripe Identity document plus selfie; Veriff 0.80 to 1.89 with monthly minimums.

verify_share_uk.label: Users needing a check per year, UK
verify_share_uk.note: Online Safety Act age assurance applies to services likely to be accessed by children. Editable.

verify_share_us.label: Users needing a check per year, US
verify_share_us.note: State app-store age laws (Utah, Texas) are in live litigation. Editable.

verify_share_eu.label: Users needing a check per year, EU

verify_share_other.label: Users needing a check per year, other

key_support_per_mau_year.label: Supporting users who manage their own keys
key_support_per_mau_year.note: Onboarding help, recovery guidance, signer integrations. What remains of the accounts line on Nostr.

ranking_fee_per_mau_year.label: A ranking or discovery provider
ranking_fee_per_mau_year.note: Web-of-trust ranking as a service. No public price list exists yet, including ours.

graph_eng_remains_share.label: Graph engineering that remains on Nostr
graph_eng_remains_share.note: Assembling feeds from relays on the client.

gdpr_program_year.label: GDPR program for a small app (EU or UK)

source.title: Legiscope: GDPR compliance cost ranges for SMEs (vendor estimate)

gdpr_program_year.note: Vendor ranges: micro 5k to 15k EUR, small 15k to 50k. Outsourced DPO alone runs 1,500 to 8,000 per month.

uk_osa_year.label: UK Online Safety Act, small or micro service

source.title: DSIT Online Safety Act enactment impact assessment, tables 49 to 52

uk_osa_year.note: Impact assessment, 2019 prices: ongoing 6,040 GBP with moderation and risk assessment, plus 7,460 GBP transition spread over three years; low is the 87 GBP basic case; high is a small high-risk service at 50,800 GBP. Converted at 1.30 USD per GBP.

dsa_year.label: EU Digital Services Act, non-VLOP platform

source.title: ACT position paper citing the Commission's DSA notice-and-action setup floor

dsa_year.note: Point of contact, legal representative outside the EU, notice-and-action, statements of reasons. The only published floor is the Commission's 1,500 EUR setup estimate.

us_privacy_year_small.label: US privacy program, below the CCPA threshold

us_privacy_year_large.label: US privacy program, at or above the CCPA threshold

ccpa_consumer_threshold.label: CCPA consumer threshold

source.title: California Attorney General: CCPA thresholds

ccpa_consumer_threshold.note: The law applies above 25M USD revenue, or 100k California consumers, or 50% of revenue from selling personal information. The model uses MAU as the proxy for consumers.

dsar_rate_per_mau_year.label: Data subject access requests per user

source.title: DataGrail citing Gartner 2023 Market Guide: cost per manually handled DSAR

dsar_rate_per_mau_year.note: 3.2 per thousand customers, attributed to DLA Piper.

dsar_cost.label: Cost of handling one request

source.title: DataGrail citing Gartner 2023 Market Guide: cost per manually handled DSAR

dsar_cost.note: Gartner's 1,524 is for a manually handled request; automated export is far cheaper.

cyber_insurance_year.label: Cyber liability insurance, small business

source.title: Insureon: cyber liability insurance cost for small businesses

cyber_insurance_year.note: Median of policies sold. Scales with data held.

breach_prob_year.label: Probability of a breach in a year
breach_prob_year.note: No per-firm annual figure is published. Hiscox reports 59% of SMEs saw an attack in twelve months, which is not a breach rate.

breach_cost_per_user.label: Breach cost per affected user

source.title: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026: global average

breach_cost_per_user.note: IBM stopped publishing a per-record figure; earlier editions ran around 150 to 165 per record for large organisations. The typical value is deliberately far below that.

breach_cost_cap.label: Breach cost cap

source.title: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026: global average

breach_cost_cap.note: The 2026 global mean. High is the US mean reported from the same edition. Expected loss is never scaled above it.

privacy_remains_share.label: Privacy program that remains on Nostr
privacy_remains_share.note: For whatever the app still retains privately.

retained_data_share.label: Personal data an app still holds on Nostr

ts_tooling_per_mau_year.label: Moderation tooling
ts_tooling_per_mau_year.note: Classifiers, queues, hash matching. Vendor pricing is per item and unpublished at small scale.

appeals_share.label: Appeals and escalation on top of review labour

moderation_remains_share.label: Moderation that remains on Nostr
moderation_remains_share.note: Illegal-content reports, app-store policy, appeals on what the app hosts. Ranking and discovery move to web of trust.

apple_rate_standard.label: Apple App Store commission, standard

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

apple_rate_standard.note: 30% worldwide; 26% under the EU terms effective 2026-10-01. Subscriptions drop to 15% after the first year, not modelled.

apple_rate_small.label: Apple App Store commission, Small Business Program

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

google_rate_standard.label: Google Play commission above 1M USD

source.title: Google Play service fees (US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30; other markets)

google_rate_standard.note: US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30: 20% new installs or 25% existing, plus 5% if Play Billing is used. Other markets 30%.

google_rate_small.label: Google Play commission on the first 1M USD

source.title: Google Play service fees (US, UK and EEA from 2026-06-30; other markets)

google_rate_small.note: 10% service fee plus 5% billing fee in the US, UK and EEA; 15% elsewhere.

store_small_threshold.label: Small-business threshold for store tiers

source.title: Apple App Store Small Business Program

store_small_threshold.note: Both stores step at 1M USD a year.

processor_rate.label: Card processor rate

source.title: Stripe pricing (US)

processor_rate.note: Stripe US 2.9%; low is Stripe UK domestic cards 1.5%; high is PayPal Checkout 3.49%.

source.title: Stripe pricing (US)

reseller_rate.label: Merchant-of-record rate

source.title: Paddle pricing (merchant of record)

reseller_rate.note: Paddle and Lemon Squeezy list 5% plus a fixed fee; the reseller is the seller and carries sales tax and VAT.

source.title: Paddle pricing (merchant of record)

avg_ticket.label: Average transaction size
avg_ticket.note: Turns revenue into a transaction count for the fixed fee. A bigger ticket means fewer fees, so low is the larger ticket.

source.title: OpenNode pricing and fees

mt_avoidance_year.label: Legal work to stay out of money-transmitter status
mt_avoidance_year.note: Counsel and structuring for in-app balances or payouts. Charged only when the app holds user balances, credits or wallets.

mt_remains_share.label: Of that legal work, what remains on Nostr
mt_remains_share.note: An app that never holds funds has far less exposure.

growth_default.label: User growth over the next year, when not given
growth_default.note: Used only for a visitor who has not said. Early-stage forecasts run far higher (Equidam finds founders forecast 120% in year one); an app with users already is held to a modest figure on purpose.

growth_decay.label: Each year's growth rate as a share of the previous year's

source.title: Equidam: benchmarks for startup revenue growth (15,000+ ventures)

growth_decay.note: Founders' own forecasts fall from 120% to 83% to 60% a year, about 0.7 each year. A doubling app is therefore about 9 times its size in year five, not 32.

migration_months.label: Months for custody to leave, once work starts
migration_months.note: Front-loaded: the share of custody gone by month m is 1 − (1 − m/M)², since the large lines (storage, compute, keys) move first and the long tail drains last. Twelve months realises two thirds of the first year's saving; twenty-four about 42% of the first and 92% of the second. Low is the slower migration, which is the smaller saving. No one-time integration cost is modelled.
